test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which harvest festival in Tripura involves traditional tribal dances and rituals after jhum cultivation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Garia Puja**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Garia Puja** is a major harvest festival celebrated in the northeastern state of **Tripura**, primarily by the **Tripuri** and **Jamatia** tribal communities.
 
• The festival is observed on the seventh day of the Hindu month of **Baishakh** (usually falling in **April**) to honor **Lord Garia**, the deity of livestock, wealth, and prosperity.
 
• It marks the successful conclusion of the **Jhum cultivation** cycle (shifting cultivation) and serves as a prayer for a prosperous new agricultural year.
 
• The ritualistic worship involves a symbolic **bamboo pole** decorated with garlands and thread, representing the deity, alongside offerings of fowls, eggs, and rice beer.
 
• A significant highlight is the **Garia dance**, where performers mimic the actions of agricultural labor and household chores through rhythmic movements and traditional music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Moatsu**

 
 
• Celebrated by the **Ao Naga** tribe of **Nagaland** in the first week of **May**.
 
• It signifies the completion of the **sowing season** and involves community singing and the sharing of rice beer.
 
 
 
• **Losar**
 
 
• Known as the **Tibetan New Year**, it is widely celebrated in **Arunachal Pradesh** (by the **Monpa** tribe), **Ladakh**, and **Sikkim**.
 
• The festivities involve religious rituals at **monasteries** and traditional dances to ward off evil spirits.
 
 
 
• **Chapchar Kut**
 
 
• This is the most important festival of **Mizoram**, celebrated during **March**.
 
• It occurs after the clearing of forests for **Jhum** (burning of trees) and features the world-renowned **Cheraw** or bamboo dance.
